svg.title: How much leaks add to the footprint of gas
svg.desc: For each kilogram of gas produced, assuming 2.3% leaks as Alvarez and colleagues found for the US supply chain in 2015: burning the rest gives 2.68 kg of CO2. On a 100-year view the leaked methane adds 0.69 kg of CO2 equivalent, 26% more; on a 20-year view it adds 1.90 kg, 71% more. Global average upstream leakage is lower, about 1% according to the IEA in 2026, and some fields are much higher.
svg.text: Per kg of gas produced: how much do leaks add?
kg CO₂e, assuming 2.3% of the gas leaks (Alvarez et al. 2018, US supply chain, 2015). My arithmetic.
Burned: 97.7% of 1 kg × 2.74 = 2.68 kg CO₂. Leaked: 2.3% × GWP. Treats the gas as pure methane.
Global average upstream leakage is lower, about 1% (IEA 2026); some fields are much higher.
Over 20 years, leaks of this size add most of the warming of burning the gas itself.
